answer: To open an earning seat, an agent leases one numbered sand-spit on a mapped river island, plants a uniquely stamped bronze gnomon there, and at a randomly assigned minute photographs the shadow the instant it touches a catalogued horizon notch. Lease serial, stamp grain, shadow angle, and that minute's river stage are posted. Shared gnomons show the same grain; studio fakes miss the ephemeris and live stage. Forging N identities needs N spit leases, N distinct castings, and N on-site timed sightings, so cost tracks scarce island ground and clock time rather than cheap key generation.
